question: Can a flat controller fitted to support demonstrations, with no supplied program, execute successful commands outside the bank of complete demonstrated schedules? How much does access to intermediate local sensors contribute?
cohort: Use the same identity-checked validation bank, first at most six worlds per program, and the same native exact-grid endpoint and legality checks as the fixed-schedule comparison. Leave each world out in turn. Fit only on the other worlds in its program. No held-out target action, endpoint, length, source code, program ID or textual instruction may enter policy decisions. Reference worlds may be decoded for independent scoring.
policy: Each support demonstration supplies its initial grid and observed primitive trajectory including terminal STOP. Record a next-action vote at every boundary including the start and STOP, conditioned on current five local Boolean predicates and suffix of at most three previous (pre-action predicates, executed action) events, with an explicit beginning sentinel. Select the most-voted action under the longest observed suffix; if current predicates were never seen, fall back to the same support bank's action-only suffix predictor. At count ties prefer STOP, then alphabetical native action name. Masked control uses the identical algorithm with all sensors set to one constant on support and target. Keep sensor votes and source-policy state flat. Both policies decide and execute iteratively with identical action limits.
termination: Compare exact final world only when the controller chooses STOP. Crash or exceeding min(512,max(32,2*maximum support trace length+8)) actions is failure. Never stop early because of the target output. A repeated identical full native world and policy history has deterministic continuation and may be stopped as a loop.
primary: Program-macro endpoint success of the sensor policy minus masked policy. Report both absolute rates, paired program-bootstrap descriptive 95% interval with 5000 replicates and RNG seed 20261120. All eligible programs count, including programs on which policies tie or both fail.
secondary: Report count/rate of target worlds where the sensor policy reaches the endpoint but NO complete trace in the other worlds can reach it on replay; report the masked count on the same subset. Verify successful traces from that subset differ from every support trace. Report cases lost as well as gained relative to the hindsight fixed-plan ceiling, exact target action trace match, cap/crash counts and coverage, and conditional-syntax descriptives. This is an evaluation of a one-level memory-based policy, not evidence for learned subcontrollers, large-model transfer or for a physical robot.
initial_observation_control: Additional comparison fixed before readout: a third policy observes the initial predicates, held constant at every later boundary on both support and query. Compare live versus this policy to separate the value of updated sensors from access to the initial observation. The fifth bit is the complement of marker-present, so exact sensor keys store the four independent bits only. A recurrent finite-action suffix may represent history; there is no learned program stack.
